items.title: Gemini Decisions API
items.snippet: Gemini Decisions API Google join Jev and OpenAI in the decision model category with "Gemini Decision 1". This new model API is almost identical to Jev: it supports the same three types of questions (yes/no, choice, and rubric-scoring) and even reuses Jev's term "Noul" for a yes/no question. It's priced the same as the GPT-6 Luna decision model: 10 cents per million input tokens, and output is free. Jev remains the cheapest of the three, at 4.2 cents per million. Jev is text (and JSON) only. Open
items.title_ar: Google تطلق Gemini Decision 1 بواجهة API منافسة
items.summary_ar: أطلقت Google موديل Gemini Decision 1 ضمن فئة decision models، وواجهته شبه مطابقة لواجهة Jev وتدعم نفس الأنواع الثلاثة من الأسئلة، وهي yes/no، choice، rubric-scoring. التسعير 10 cents لكل مليون input token مع output مجاني، بينما يبقى Jev الأرخص بسعر 4.2 cents لكل مليون، ويدعم النص وJSON فقط.
items.why_ar: يمكنه تجربة واجهة decision API جديدة ومقارنة تكلفتها مع الخيارات الحالية في حلول الـ agents.
items.title_en: Google launches Gemini Decision 1 with a competing decision API
items.summary_en: Google released Gemini Decision 1 in the decision model category, with an API almost identical to Jev and the same three question types: yes/no, choice, and rubric-scoring. It costs 10 cents per million input tokens with free output, while Jev remains cheapest at 4.2 cents per million and supports text and JSON only.
items.why_en: This engineer can test a new decision API right away and compare its cost against current options for agent workflows.

items.title: aws-emulator
items.snippet: aws-emulator Finally, an official emulator from AWS to run tests against a local clone of their many different services without having to provision a paid API key to do so. It's written in Rust by a huge swarm of agents - 29,684 commits in the first three weeks of the project. Swaminathan (Swami) Sivasubramanian wrote about how it came to be in a guest post on Werner Vogels' blog. It currently requires Docker to run on macOS or Windows. I'm hoping they fix that in the future - it would be great
items.title_ar: AWS تطلق emulator رسمي مكتوب بلغة Rust
items.summary_ar: أطلقت AWS emulator رسمي يعمل كنسخة محلية من خدماتها لتشغيل الاختبارات دون الحاجة إلى API key مدفوع. كُتب المشروع بلغة Rust عبر swarm كبير من agents مع 29,684 commits خلال أول ثلاثة أسابيع. القيد الحالي هو الحاجة إلى Docker على macOS وWindows، وهو ما يأمل المطور إصلاحه مستقبلاً.
items.why_ar: يمكنه تجربة الاختبار المحلي لخدمات AWS فوراً وتقليل تكلفة بيئات التطوير.
items.title_en: AWS releases an official Rust-based emulator for its services
items.summary_en: AWS released an official emulator that runs a local clone of its services so tests can run without a paid API key. The project was written in Rust by a large swarm of agents, with 29,684 commits in its first three weeks. It currently requires Docker on macOS and Windows, a limitation the author hopes will be fixed later.
items.why_en: This engineer can immediately test AWS services locally and reduce development environment costs.

items.title: SteerDistill: Quantizing LLM Agents via Closed-Loop Teacher Steering
items.snippet: Low-bit quantization reduces the inference cost of LLM agents but can compromise task success. Examining failed rollouts, we find that quantized agents overlook task requirements or environmental conditions, producing environment transitions that diverge from successful full-precision references. Correcting these behavioral divergences remains difficult: offline data may miss the student's failure contexts, while its own rollouts may provide few correct responses in those contexts. We introduce SteerDistill, a quantization-aware distillation method in which a full-precision teacher guides the student to revise failed responses and iteratively refines its guidance using feedback from student
items.title_ar: SteerDistill: تكميم وكلاء LLM عبر توجيه المعلم في حلقة مغلقة
items.summary_ar: تعالج الورقة فقدان دقة وكلاء LLM بعد quantization منخفض البت، إذ تتجاوز النماذج المكمّمة متطلبات المهمة أو شروط البيئة. تقدم SteerDistill طريقة distillation واعية بالتكميم، حيث يوجه teacher بكامل الدقة الـ student لمراجعة الاستجابات الفاشلة ويحسن التوجيه تدريجياً بناءً على feedback منه. الهدف تقليل تكلفة inference مع الحفاظ على نسبة نجاح المهام
items.why_ar: إذا كنت تنشر agents بتكلفة inference عالية فهذا يوضح كيف تحافظ على الجودة عند تصغير الموديل
items.title_en: SteerDistill: quantizing LLM agents via closed-loop teacher steering
items.summary_en: The paper addresses the loss of task success when low-bit quantization is applied to LLM agents, which overlook task requirements or environment conditions. It introduces SteerDistill, a quantization-aware distillation method where a full-precision teacher guides the student to revise failed responses and iteratively refines that guidance using student feedback. The goal is to reduce inference cost while preserving task success.
items.why_en: If you deploy agents with high inference costs, this shows how to keep task success while shrinking the model.

items.title: Read Less, Solve More: Token-Efficient Sparse Reading of External Content for AI Agents
items.snippet: Web-facing AI agents repeatedly access webpages, documents, repositories, and tool responses, yet reading interfaces often expose entire objects when only sparse evidence is needed. This over-reading increases token and latency costs and can dilute relevant evidence. We present SparseRead, a reusable reading control layer that governs content admission without modifying the agent model. Its Read Intent Protocol tracks evolving needs and source coverage; Adaptive Reader Backends select how evidence is located and exposed; and the Budgeted Read Gate bounds cumulative raw exposure per episode with faithful full-view fallback. A unified Reader interface supports interchangeable evidence acquisit
items.title_ar: SparseRead: قراءة متناثرة وفعالة في الرموز لمحتوى الوكلاء الخارجي
items.summary_ar: تعرض الورقة SparseRead وهي طبقة تحكم في القراءة تنظم دخول المحتوى من صفحات الويب والوثائق والمستودعات دون تعديل موديل الوكيل. تتبع Read Intent Protocol الاحتياجات المتغيرة وتغطية المصادر، بينما تختار Adaptive Reader Backends طريقة تحديد الدليل وعرضه. وتحدد Budgeted Read Gate كمية المحتوى الخام المعروضة لكل episode مع fallback كامل عند الحاجة
items.why_ar: أي وكيل يقرأ مستندات وصفحات بشكل متكرر يدفع تكلفة tokens وlatency زائدة وهذا يمس عملك مباشرة
items.title_en: SparseRead: token-efficient sparse reading of external content for agents
items.summary_en: The paper introduces SparseRead, a reusable reading control layer that governs how agents admit content from webpages, documents, and repositories without modifying the agent model. Its Read Intent Protocol tracks evolving needs and source coverage, while Adaptive Reader Backends select how evidence is located and exposed. A Budgeted Read Gate bounds raw exposure per episode, with full-view fallback when needed.
items.why_en: Any agent repeatedly reading documents or pages pays extra token and latency cost, which is directly relevant to your work.

items.title: Precision on Demand: Escalating Weight Bits at Uncertain Decoding Steps in a Small Local Model
items.snippet: Local decoding usually fixes one weight precision for the whole generation. We study a different allocation: store 8-bit weights, decode with their top 4 bits, and redo a step at 8 bits only when the low-precision output distribution looks uncertain (entropy above a threshold or a small top-two margin). Quantization is simulated, the model is Qwen3-0.6B, and the benchmark is GSM8K. Cost is counted in weight bytes read per token. On 36724 replayed steps the entropy of the low pass ranks argmax flips with AUC 0.93. At a 15% escalation budget it catches 78% of flips and the margin gate 94%, against the 15% expected for a random gate of equal rate (a computed expectation, not a run). In 150 live
items.title_ar: Precision on Demand: تصعيد دقة الأوزان عند خطوات التوليد غير المؤكدة
items.summary_ar: يقترح البحث تخزين الأوزان بدقة 8-bit وفك الترميز بأعلى 4 bits فقط، ثم إعادة الخطوة بدقة 8-bit عند عدم اليقين في توزيع المخرجات. على Qwen3-0.6B وGSM8K، يلتقط margin gate نسبة 94% من تغيرات argmax عند ميزانية تصعيد 15%، مقابل 15% متوقعة للاختيار العشوائي. النتائج مبنية على محاكاة للتكميم وعلى 36724 خطوة معاد تشغيلها.
items.why_ar: يقدم طريقة عملية لموازنة الذاكرة والحوسبة مقابل الدقة في الموديلات الصغيرة المشغلة محلياً.
items.title_en: Precision on Demand: Escalating Weight Bits for Small Local Models
items.summary_en: The paper stores 8-bit weights but decodes with only their top 4 bits, redoing a step at 8 bits when the low-precision output looks uncertain. On Qwen3-0.6B with GSM8K, a margin gate catches 94% of argmax flips at a 15% escalation budget, versus an expected 15% for a random gate. The results come from simulated quantization over 36724 replayed steps, and the source text is truncated before the live results.
items.why_en: It offers a practical way to trade memory and compute for accuracy in small local models.

items.title: Bits or permutations? Spending a fixed inference budget on weight precision or on option-order averaging in small local language models
items.snippet: Local language models can save memory by storing weights in fewer bits, and they can reduce sensitivity to the order of answer options by averaging a few reorderings. We ask whether the first makes the second worse, and which is the cheaper way to spend a fixed budget. On Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B with simulated round-to-nearest weight quantization (8, 6, 4 and 3 bits, fp16 reference), read from the logits of the letters A to D on ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, MMLU and HellaSwag (300 items each), 6 bits lose no accuracy against fp16 (they score +1.8 (+1.0 to +2.5) and +0.9 (+0.3 to +1.5) points higher, which we do not explain), and 8 bits change it by -0.7 (-1.1 to -0.3) and -0.4 (-0.7 to -0.2) p
items.title_ar: Bits أم Permutations: أيهما أنفع لميزانية inference ثابتة؟
items.summary_ar: تقارن الورقة بين خفض دقة الأوزان ومتوسط ترتيبات خيارات الإجابة لتقليل حساسية الموديلات الصغيرة لترتيب الخيارات. على Qwen3-0.6B وQwen3-1.7B وعدة benchmarks، لم يسجل 6-bit أي خسارة في الدقة مقارنة بـ fp16، بينما أدى 8-bit إلى تغيير طفيف في الدقة.
items.why_ar: يساعد على اختيار طريقة أرخص لتحسين الموديلات المحلية دون خسارة كبيرة في الجودة.
items.title_en: Bits or permutations? Spending a fixed inference budget on small models
items.summary_en: The paper compares spending a fixed inference budget on weight precision versus averaging over reordered answer options in small Qwen3 models. On ARC, MMLU and HellaSwag, 6-bit weights showed no accuracy loss against fp16, while 8-bit weights changed scores slightly. The evaluation uses 300 items per benchmark and reads answer letter logits.
items.why_en: It gives a data-driven guide for allocating limited compute between quantization and option-order averaging in local models.

items.title: Evolving Infra: Agent-Adaptive LLM Serving at Scale
items.snippet: Agentic workloads are a major source of LLM inference demand. Existing prefill--decode (PD) disaggregated serving systems offer limited flexibility for runtime adaptation of compute allocation and KV cache management, and rely on coarse signals that only partly capture the diverse and dynamic agent workload. These limitations lead to load imbalance between prefill and decode nodes and eviction of KV caches that agents will reuse. We present Evolving Infra, an agent-adaptive serving framework that adapts compute allocation to agent workloads and KV cache management to agent context management at runtime. We decouple compute allocation from key--value (KV) cache management, allowing nodes to s
items.title_ar: Evolving Infra: خدمة LLM متكيفة مع الوكلاء على نطاق واسع
items.summary_ar: تعرض الورقة Evolving Infra وهو إطار serving يكيّف تخصيص compute وإدارة KV cache حسب workload الوكلاء أثناء التشغيل. تفصل الورقة تخصيص الحوسبة عن إدارة KV cache لتجنب اختلال التحميل بين nodes الـ prefill والـ decode والإخراج المبكر لـ caches يعيد الوكلاء استخدامها. تستهدف النتيجة تحسين كفاءة inference للأحمال الوكيلية
items.why_ar: إذا كنت تشغّل agents على بنيتك التحتية فإدارة KV cache وتوزيع الحمل تؤثر مباشرة على التكلفة والـ latency
items.title_en: Evolving Infra: agent-adaptive LLM serving at scale
items.summary_en: The paper presents Evolving Infra, a serving framework that adapts compute allocation and KV cache management to agent workloads at runtime. It decouples compute allocation from KV cache management to avoid load imbalance between prefill and decode nodes and to stop eviction of caches that agents will reuse. The goal is more efficient inference for agentic workloads.
items.why_en: If you run agent workloads on your own infrastructure, KV cache and load balancing directly affect cost and latency.

items.title: Module-Aware Optimization for Graph Neural Networks
items.snippet: Different optimizers impose different geometries on parameter updates. Adaptive methods such as Adam and AdamW use coordinate-wise updates, while matrix-aware optimizers such as Muon utilize weight-matrix structure through orthogonalized updates. For Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), however, the effective geometry of its weight matrices is shaped not only by its learned channel-mixing weights, but also by the graph-propagated representations it acts on. Thus, even if an update is well normalized as a matrix, its effect on the layer output can be amplified when applied to graph-propagated features. To address this gap, we introduce GraphMuon, a graph-aware optimizer that adapts Muon's matrix upd
items.title_ar: GraphMuon: تحسين Muon لشبكات Graph Neural Networks
items.summary_ar: يقدم الباحثون GraphMuon، وهو optimizer يكيّف تحديثات Muon المعتمدة على matrix structure مع الخصائص المنتشرة عبر الرسم البياني. الفكرة أن التحديث المُوزون جيداً كمصفوفة قد يتضخم أثره على ناتج الطبقة عند تطبيقه على graph-propagated features.
items.why_ar: يفيد المهندس إذا كان يدرب نماذج GNN لكشف الاحتيال أو تحليل العلاقات بين الحسابات، لأنه يقدم طريقة تدريب مختلفة لهذه النماذج.
items.title_en: GraphMuon: Module-Aware Optimization for Graph Neural Networks
items.summary_en: The paper introduces GraphMuon, a graph-aware optimizer that adapts Muon's matrix update to GNNs. It argues that graph propagation can amplify the effect of well-normalized updates on layer outputs.
items.why_en: It may help if you train graph models for fraud detection or account-relationship analysis at the bank.

items.title: PolyRoute: A Twelve-Language and Code-Mixed Benchmark for Typed-Decision Routing, with Baselines and a Leaderboard
items.snippet: Typed-decision encoders answer a question about a text in one forward pass, but their behaviour outside English is rarely measured on a fixed yardstick. We release PolyRoute: 322 native-language support messages in 12 languages and 9 writing systems, 156 code-mixed or romanised messages (Hinglish, Spanglish, Arabizi), 967 optional native training rows, and a protocol for a three-way department-routing decision. items.title_ar: PolyRoute: بنشمارك متعدد اللغات لتوجيه طلبات الدعم بلغات مختلطة
items.summary_ar: تقدم الورقة PolyRoute وهو benchmark يضم 322 رسالة دعم بـ12 لغة وتسعة أنظمة كتابة، إضافة إلى 156 رسالة code-mixed أو romanised مثل Hinglish وSpanglish وArabizi. يحدد البحث protocol لقرار توجيه ثلاثي إلى الأقسام، وتعتمد الـ labels على Qwen3.8-27B مع مراجعة ثانية مستقلة. ويضم الـ leaderboard 13 نظاماً مع نتائج أساسية للمقارنة

items.title_en: PolyRoute: a twelve-language benchmark for typed-decision routing
items.summary_en: The paper releases PolyRoute, a benchmark with 322 native support messages in 12 languages and 9 writing systems, plus 156 code-mixed or romanised messages such as Hinglish, Spanglish, and Arabizi. It defines a three-way department-routing protocol with labels from Qwen3.8-27B and a blind second pass. A leaderboard of 13 systems provides baselines for comparison.
items.why_en: Routing customer messages written in mixed or romanised languages is directly relevant to banking support systems.

items.title: CARTBench: Rubric-Based Evaluation of Shopping Advice for Complex and Ambiguous Requests with Timelines
items.snippet: Large language model (LLM) shopping assistants now recommend products in multi-turn conversations. However, reliable evaluation faces Data scarcity and Difficulty Standardizing Criteria. To address these obstacles, we introduce CARTBench for CART (Complex and Ambiguous Requests with Timelines). For Data scarcity, we curate cases from real commercial shopping needs across 17 retail domains, pairing timestamped dialogue with 1,603 product records. For Difficulty Standardizing Criteria, we develop case-specific rubrics guided by Ideal Response Principles, distilled from excellent replies manually selected from successfully completed orders. items.title_ar: CARTBench: تقييم نصائح مساعدي التسوق بالـ LLM عبر rubrics
items.summary_ar: يقدم الباحثون CARTBench، وهو benchmark لتقييم نصائح التسوق في محادثات متعددة الأدوار، ويضم 1,603 product records عبر 17 retail domains. يعتمد التقييم على rubrics خاصة بكل حالة مستمدة من ردود مثالية اختيرت يدوياً.
items.why_ar: يفيد في بناء معايير تقييم منهجية لأي مساعد LLM يتعامل مع طلبات غامضة في خدمة العملاء المصرفية.
items.title_en: CARTBench: Rubric-Based Evaluation of Shopping Advice with Timelines
items.summary_en: CARTBench is a benchmark for evaluating LLM shopping assistants in multi-turn conversations, with 1,603 product records across 17 retail domains. It uses case-specific rubrics derived from manually selected ideal replies.
items.why_en: The rubric-based method transfers directly to judging LLM assistants that handle ambiguous customer requests.
